newsitem.title: USA: VideoLan receives US Defense Dept orders.
newsitem.headline: VideoLan receives US Defense Dept orders.

text.p: VideoLan Technologies Inc on Tuesday said it has received multiple independent orders for its VL2000 desktop video and visual information network for the Defense Department.

The orders reflect and confirm the Defense Department's announced intentions to spend up to $250 million on upgraded video conferencing capabilities and independently projected spending on video archiving and networking equipment of as much as another $250 million in 1997 and $350 million in 1998.

Installations include the US Air Force Training Command at Maxwell AFB, Ala., The US Army Training Command at Ft. Benning, Ga., and to video communications for senior commanders in undisclosed commands, the company said.
The orders are independent of each other and are networks that have been installed and in operation or are undergoing installation at present.
VideoLan Technologies Inc develops video conferencing and video broadcast products based upon its Metallic Fiber transmission and broadband switching technology.
